name: Passcode is never actually enforced (no lock screen)
whatItIs: Modern AppLock (submodules/AppLock, AppLockState, PasscodeUI) keeps a LockState with isManuallyLocked, autolockTimeout and a monotonic applicationActivityTimestamp, and presents a full-screen PasscodeEntryController over the window whenever isAppLocked() is true on launch or on becoming active; failed attempts are counted and rate-limited.
whyItMatters: We ship a complete Passcode Lock settings screen (TGPrivacyViewController.m: TGPasscodeViewController, digest + TGPasscodeAutoLockSeconds) but nothing in AppDelegate.m or RootViewController.m ever reads passcodeIsSet/autoLockSeconds. A user who turns the passcode on gets zero protection - the app opens straight into the chat list. That is worse than not offering the feature. Also the digest lives in NSUserDefaults, which is world-readable on a jailbroken device; it belongs in the keychain.
whereItGoes: AppDelegate.m applicationDidBecomeActive/didFinishLaunching plus a new full-screen keypad overlay window; the existing +passcodeMatches: is the check. Telegraph (twelve/Telegraph) has a passcode lock window to copy the structure from.
tdlib: none - purely client-local, no TDLib call involved

name: App-switcher snapshot not covered when locked
whatItIs: AppLock installs a LockedWindowCoveringView with a blurred snapshot on willResignActive so iOS's suspend screenshot never shows chat content.
whyItMatters: iOS 6 caches a PNG of the last frame under the app's Library/Caches/Snapshots on suspend. With a passcode set, that snapshot leaks the open conversation to anyone who double-taps home, and the file persists on disk. Cheap fix, real leak.
whereItGoes: AppDelegate.m applicationWillResignActive - add an opaque logo view to the key window, remove it on didBecomeActive. Only meaningful together with the lock-enforcement gap above.

name: VoiceOver labels and traits
whatItIs: Modern Telegram annotates nearly every node: chat list rows read as "name, message, time, N unread", bubbles expose accessibilityLabel plus custom actions (reply, forward, delete), and every icon-only bar button has a label.
whyItMatters: There is not a single accessibilityLabel or isAccessibilityElement in our 88k lines. VoiceOver on iOS 6 is complete and works fine on a 4S, but our custom-drawn ChatViewCell and TGChatListViewController cells are drawn into one CALayer, so a blind user hears nothing usable and icon-only buttons (attach, mic, mute icon, back chevron) announce as "Button". This is the one accessibility item that a real user actually loses.
whereItGoes: ChatViewCell.m and TGChatListViewController.m cell configure methods (set isAccessibilityElement=YES and compose the label from data we already have), plus the toolbar/nav buttons in TGChatViewController.m, TGTabBar.m and TGActionSheet.m.
tdlib: none - all data already parsed into our cell dictionaries

name: Message text size setting
whatItIs: PresentationData carries a user-chosen fontSize applied to all message text; Settings > Appearance has a live-preview slider. The 2013 client had the same thing as "Message Text Size".
whyItMatters: Our fonts are hard-coded, and on a 3.5" 320x480 screen the default bubble text is the single most common thing users want bigger or smaller. It is also the only realistic accessibility affordance on iOS 6, which has no Dynamic Type at all.
whereItGoes: TGTheme.h/.m as a font-size token read from NSUserDefaults, a slider or a 5-row radio list in TGSettingsViewController.m Appearance page, and a height-cache invalidation in ChatViewCell/TGChatViewController.

name: Receive files from other apps ("Open in Telegram")
whatItIs: The modern app has a Share Extension so any app can send a photo, document or URL into a chat via ShareController.
whyItMatters: iOS 6 has no app extensions, but it has the document-interaction handoff the 2013 app used: declare CFBundleDocumentTypes, get the file at application:openURL: as a file:// URL, and show a chat picker. Today our Info.plist declares only the telegram:// URL scheme and no document types, so Telegram never appears in any other app's "Open In" list - there is no way at all to get a file from Safari, Photos or Mail into a chat.
whereItGoes: src/Info.plist CFBundleDocumentTypes (public.image, public.movie, public.data, public.url), AppDelegate.m handleOpenURL: branch for file URLs, then reuse the existing TGForwardPicker to choose the destination chat.
tdlib: sendMessage / inputMessageDocument / inputMessagePhoto - already wrapped in TGClient+Messages and TGClient+MessageContent

name: Send media out of Telegram (Open In / share sheet)
whatItIs: Modern Telegram's media viewer and document bubbles offer a system share sheet: save, open in another app, copy link.
whyItMatters: UIActivityViewController exists on iOS 6 and we already use it once (TGContactsViewController.m:1037), but nowhere in the chat: a received photo, video or document is a dead end - it cannot be saved to the camera roll or opened in another app. UIDocumentInteractionController is the iOS 6 way to do the "Open In" half.
whereItGoes: The message action sheet in TGChatViewController.m and the full-screen media viewer; downloaded file paths already come back from TGClient+Files.
tdlib: downloadFile - wrapped; getSuggestedFileName / getFileMimeType would tidy the filename but are optional

name: Photo library permission denial guidance
whatItIs: submodules/DeviceAccess centralises camera/microphone/photos/contacts checks and shows a "go to Settings > Privacy" alert when access was refused.
whyItMatters: We do this correctly for camera (TGQRViewController.m, TGVideoRecorder.m) and microphone (TGVoiceRecorder.m) but not for Photos: a user who denied photo access gets a silently empty UIImagePickerController from the attach menu with no explanation, which reads as a broken app.
whereItGoes: Wherever UIImagePickerController is presented - TGChatViewController.m, TGProfileViewController.m, TGSettingsViewController.m, TGStoriesViewController.m - guarded by +[ALAssetsLibrary authorizationStatus], reusing the alert wording already in TGQRViewController.m.

name: Home-screen quick actions, widgets and a share extension
whatItIs: 3D Touch shortcut items (Saved Messages, top contacts, compose), the WidgetItems/WidgetItemsUtils home-screen widget, and the Share/Notification-Service extensions.
whyItMatters: Nothing to build - recorded so the area is closed. The 4S has no 3D Touch hardware, and iOS 6 predates app extensions (introduced in iOS 8) and WidgetKit entirely; there is no Today view for third-party apps either. The only usable substitutes are the document-type handoff and the telegram:// URL scheme, both covered above.
whereItGoes: n/a

name: Sign-up screen for brand new accounts
whatItIs: AuthorizationSequenceSignUpController: after the code is accepted for a phone number that has no account, Telegram asks for first name, last name and an optional avatar, showing the terms of service (as a must-accept popup when showPopup is set, with a minimum-age confirmation).
whyItMatters: Right now a new user is permanently stuck. TGClient maps authorizationStateWaitRegistration to TGAuthStateWaitRegistration, but AppDelegate's onAuthState switch falls into `default: break`, so the code screen just freezes with no error. Only existing accounts can log in.
whereItGoes: New TGLoginStepRegistration in src/TGLoginViewController.m (two text fields reusing the existing input chrome, terms shown via TGAlertView), plus a case in the switch at src/AppDelegate.m:105.
tdlib: setProfilePhoto for the optional avatar - already wrapped in TGClient+Account

name: Auth state machine ignores the email, other-device and premium-purchase states
whatItIs: Modern AuthorizationSequenceController drives every screen off the authorization state, including authorizationStateWaitEmailAddress, WaitEmailCode, WaitOtherDeviceConfirmation and WaitPremiumPurchase.
whyItMatters: TGClient.m -handleAuthState: returns early on any state it does not recognise (the `else { return; }` at line 426), so those four never reach the UI. Our email and QR steps only appear when the user taps a button; when the server pushes an email second factor after the code, or when the QR is scanned on the other device, the screen does not move. The login email flow is fully wrapped but effectively unreachable in the server-driven direction.
whereItGoes: src/TGClient.h TGAuthState enum, src/TGClient.m:403 -handleAuthState:, and the switch in src/AppDelegate.m:105 routing to the existing showEmailStep/showEmailCodeStep/showQrStep methods in TGLoginViewController.m.
tdlib: authorizationStateWaitEmailAddress / WaitEmailCode / WaitOtherDeviceConfirmation - parsing only; setAuthenticationEmailAddress, checkAuthenticationEmailCode and requestQrCodeLogin are already wrapped (TGClient+Account.h)

name: Word and phrase login codes are untypable
whatItIs: TDLib now issues authenticationCodeTypeSmsWord and SmsPhrase, where the login code is a word or a short phrase (with a first_letter hint), not digits. Modern's code entry switches to a text field for those cases.
whyItMatters: showCodeStepWithPhoneNumber hardcodes UIKeyboardTypeNumberPad (TGLoginViewController.m:733) and the length check expects digits, so on any account Telegram routes to a word code, the user physically cannot enter it and login is dead. TGAccountCodeDescription already recognises the two type names but tells the user it sent 'an SMS with the code'.
whereItGoes: src/TGLoginViewController.m -showCodeStepWithPhoneNumber:/-applyCodeInfo:, keyed off the existing "type" field; wording in TGAccountCodeDescription at src/TGClient+Account.m:55.
tdlib: authenticationCodeTypeSmsWord / SmsPhrase first_letter - already parsed in TGClient+Account.m, just not surfaced in the info dictionary

name: Account reset when the 2FA password is lost
whatItIs: AuthorizationSequenceAwaitingAccountResetController: when the user has a cloud password but no working recovery email, Telegram offers to delete and reset the account after a waiting period, showing a live countdown until the reset can be confirmed.
whyItMatters: The password step offers only 'Forgot password?', which mails a recovery code. A user with no recovery email hits a dead end and can never get back into their number, which is the exact situation this screen exists for.
whereItGoes: New branch off TGLoginStepPassword in src/TGLoginViewController.m (the recovery path around line 783 already exists), reusing the countdown timer machinery already there for resend.
tdlib: deleteAccount - wrapped as -deleteAccountWithReason:password:completion: (TGClient+Privacy.h:182); it also works in authorizationStateWaitPassword and returns the pending wait period in the error text

name: Authorising another device by scanning its QR code
whatItIs: Scanning a tg://login?token= QR shown by a desktop or web client, then confirming a sheet that names the device, app, IP and location before granting the session.
whyItMatters: This is the only way to sign in to Telegram Desktop or Web from this phone, and it is half-built: -confirmQrCodeLogin: is wrapped in TGClient+Account.m:401 with no caller anywhere in src. TGQRViewController recognises the 'login' path component (line 332) but then just prints the URL as text, so the scan silently does nothing useful.
whereItGoes: src/TGQRViewController.m, the tg:// handling near line 332 - call -confirmQrCodeLogin: and present the returned session dictionary in a TGActionSheet before confirming.

name: Unconfirmed new-login banner
whatItIs: When a new session signs in, modern Telegram puts a banner at the top of the chat list, 'New login from <device>', with Confirm and Terminate actions, so a stolen SMS code can be caught within the grace window.
whyItMatters: -unconfirmedSessionsWithCompletion: exists (TGClient+Privacy.h:77) and has no caller outside the Sessions screen; the isUnconfirmed flag is parsed in two places and shown nowhere prominent. Without the banner the user only learns of an intrusion if they happen to open Settings, Sessions.
whereItGoes: src/TGChatListViewController.m as a header view above the list, actions calling the already-wrapped -confirmSession: and -terminateSession:.
tdlib: getActiveSessions / confirmSession / terminateSession - all wrapped in TGClient+Privacy.h
updateUnconfirmedSession - needs an update hook in TGClient.m

name: Multiple accounts on one device
whatItIs: Modern Telegram keeps several logged-in accounts side by side, switchable from the settings header, with per-account unread badges and notifications, and an Add Account entry that re-enters the login sequence without logging the current account out.
whyItMatters: Anyone with a personal and a work number has to log out and back in, re-entering an SMS code every switch, and loses the local database each time. It is the single largest structural gap in this area.
whereItGoes: TGClient is a singleton around one td_json_client (src/TGClient.m); this needs a client-per-account registry, per-account TDLib database directories, and a switcher row in src/TGSettingsViewController.m. Telegraph at /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/twelve/Telegraph/ predates multi-account and offers no help here.
tdlib: td_json_client_create per account, plus routing every existing request/update path through the active client - none of this is wrapped; TGClient assumes one instance throughout

name: Inline keyboard under message bubbles
whatItIs: Modern clients draw the message's inline keyboard as rows of full-width buttons attached under the bubble, and route a tap to getCallbackQueryAnswer (toast/alert/url), openMessageContent for url buttons, getLoginUrlInfo for login buttons, or a switch-inline hand-off.
whyItMatters: Almost every bot in Telegram is driven by inline buttons. Without rendering them, bot messages arrive as text that references buttons the user can never press, which makes bots functionally unusable rather than merely degraded.
whereItGoes: ChatViewCell.m bubble layout plus a tap route in TGChatViewController.m; the whole API is already in TGClient+Bots.h (inlineKeyboardRowsForMessage:, pressCallbackButton:...) and TGClient+WebLinks.h (loginUrlInfoForButton:). Nothing in src/ imports TGClient+Bots.h today. Telegraph has the button geometry in TGModernConversationKeyboardView.h.

name: Slash-command autocomplete panel
whatItIs: Typing '/' in a chat that has bots pops a list of commands (command + description + bot avatar) above the input bar; picking one inserts it, and in groups it appends @botname when several bots share the command.
whyItMatters: It is the only discoverable way to use a command bot. Users otherwise have to know the exact command string by heart.
whereItGoes: A new overlay table above the input bar in TGChatViewController.m, fed by botCommandsForUser:matchingPrefix:completion:. Telegraph implements exactly this as TGModernConversationCommandsAssociatedPanel + TGCommandPanelCell, a cheap port.

name: Custom reply keyboard panel
whatItIs: replyMarkupShowKeyboard replaces the system keyboard with a grid of bot-supplied buttons, honouring resize, one-time and persistent, plus a custom input placeholder; forceReply focuses the input bar with the bot's placeholder and a pre-set reply target.
whyItMatters: Service and utility bots (delivery, banking, support) drive their entire flow from the reply keyboard. Without it those chats are dead ends: the bot asks the user to press a button that is not on screen.
whereItGoes: New TGBotKeyboardView presented in the input accessory slot of TGChatViewController.m, with a keyboard-toggle button in the input bar. Telegraph has TGCommandKeyboardView.h/.m doing precisely this against the same button model.
tdlib: sendMessage of the plain button text - wrapped

name: Reply-keyboard request buttons (share phone / location / users / chat)
whatItIs: Keyboard buttons of kind requestPhoneNumber, requestLocation, requestUsers and requestChat ask a confirmation, then answer the bot with shareUsersWithBot / shareChatWithBot or a contact/location message.
whyItMatters: This is how bots do login-by-phone and channel/group hand-off. A pressed request button that silently does nothing looks like a broken client.
whereItGoes: Handled inside the reply-keyboard panel in TGChatViewController.m; confirmation via the existing TGActionSheet, and the user/chat pick via the existing TGForwardPicker and TGContactsViewController.

name: Inline query results (@bot query in the input bar)
whatItIs: Typing '@botname query' opens a results panel above the input bar: a media grid for photo/gif/sticker results, a list for article results, paged with nextOffset, with a switch-to-PM header button when the bot asks for one. Selecting a result sends it as a via-bot message.
whyItMatters: @gif, @pic, @vid and every search bot live here; it is also the only path to sending a GIF from Telegram's own inline provider. On a 2013-styled client @gif is a period-correct feature that users will look for.
whereItGoes: New panel view in TGChatViewController.m plus a compact grid built on the existing TGStickerPanelView-style paging scroll (no UICollectionView on iOS 6). Telegraph has the full model layer as TGBotContextResults / TGInlineBotsInputPanel, portable with the layout swapped.

name: Recent inline bots '@' suggestion list
whatItIs: A bare '@' in an empty input bar lists the inline bots the user recently used, so the next query starts with one tap.
whyItMatters: Without it inline mode is only reachable by typing a username from memory, which few users do.
whereItGoes: Same overlay table as the slash-command panel in TGChatViewController.m, different data source.

name: START button in an empty bot chat and bot deep links
whatItIs: An empty bot conversation replaces the input bar with a full-width START button that sends /start with the deep-link payload; t.me/bot?start=xyz links open the chat and start it.
whyItMatters: It is the entry point to every bot. Today a fresh bot chat gives the user a text field and no indication that /start is required, and shared bot links do nothing.
whereItGoes: Input-bar swap in TGChatViewController.m, link handling in the existing deep-link route (TGClient+WebLinks consumers) in AppDelegate.m / RootViewController.m.
tdlib: getInternalLinkType botStart - wrapped as botStartLinkInfo: / openBotStartLink:

name: Bot profile: description, about and command list
whatItIs: A bot's profile shows its description and short description instead of bio/last-seen, lists its commands, and offers Share, Add to Group and Settings actions; the chat header shows the bot description before the first message.
whyItMatters: Users decide whether to trust and how to use a bot from this screen. Right now a bot renders as an ordinary user with an empty profile.
whereItGoes: TGProfileViewController.m section builder, plus an intro block at the top of an empty bot chat in TGChatViewController.m. Telegraph has TGBotUserInfoController and TGBotConversationHeaderView for both.

name: 'via @bot' attribution and bot service messages
whatItIs: Messages sent through an inline bot carry a 'via @botname' suffix in the header; bot service events (write access allowed, users shared, chat shared, web app data sent) render as grey service lines.
whyItMatters: Without the attribution a forwarded inline result looks like the sender made it; without the service text those events render as blank or 'unsupported' rows in the middle of a bot conversation.
whereItGoes: ChatViewCell.m header line and the service-message branch in TGChatViewController.m. Both helpers already exist and are simply never called: viaBotForMessage:completion: and botServiceTextForMessage:.

name: Bot write-access consent sheet
whatItIs: Before a bot may message the user outside a started chat, the client asks for consent and calls allowBotToSendMessages.
whyItMatters: Several link and login flows stall silently at this prompt; it is also the only user-visible control over unsolicited bot messages.
whereItGoes: A TGActionSheet raised from the bot-start / link-open path in TGChatViewController.m.

name: Bot menu button (command-menu mode)
whatItIs: A labelled button to the left of the input bar. When the bot set no web-app URL it opens the command list; when it set a URL modern clients launch the mini app.
whyItMatters: For command bots this is the visible affordance for the command list, and it costs one call. The web-app variant is not reachable here, so the button should simply fall back to the command menu.
whereItGoes: Input bar in TGChatViewController.m, sharing the command panel from the autocomplete gap; menuButtonForBot:completion: already returns text+url.

name: Similar bots section on a bot profile
whatItIs: A 'Similar bots' row set on a bot's profile listing related bots with a total count.
whyItMatters: Minor but free discovery; it is the only in-app way to find alternatives to a bot.
whereItGoes: One extra section in TGProfileViewController.m using similarBotsFor:completion:, rendered like the existing common-groups rows.

name: Mini apps / web apps and attachment-menu bots
whatItIs: openWebApp returns an https URL rendered in an in-app browser with the telegram-web-app.js bridge, backButton/mainButton chrome, theme params and sendWebAppData round-trips; attachment-menu bots are the same thing behind icons in the attach sheet.
whyItMatters: A large slice of modern bot functionality lives here, but it is genuinely unreachable and the existing 'blocked' bucket is correct.
whereItGoes: Nowhere. Confirmed blocked: no WKWebView on iOS 6.1.3, and UIWebView's 2013 JavaScriptCore cannot run today's mini-app bundles (ES6+, modern DOM APIs) nor host the JS bridge; the attachment-bot icons would be dead buttons. Web-app inline keyboard buttons should degrade to opening the URL in Safari rather than doing nothing.
tdlib: openWebApp / closeWebApp / sendWebAppData - not wrapped, deliberately

name: Call tones: ringback, ringtone, busy, connecting, ended
whatItIs: Modern TelegramCallsUI/PresentationCallToneData.swift plays a distinct looped tone per call state - ringback while the other side rings, a ringtone plus vibration on an incoming call, busy/failed on rejection, and a short end tone on hang-up, all through the call audio session.
whyItMatters: Right now an incoming call takes over the screen in complete silence and an outgoing call gives no audible feedback at all: TGCall.mm and TGCallViewController.m contain no AudioServices/AVAudioPlayer/vibration code whatsoever. A phone that rings silently is effectively a phone that misses every call.
whereItGoes: TGCall.mm state transitions (pending/exchangingKeys/ready/discarded) driving a small tone player; UI hook in TGCallViewController.m. Telegraph (twelve/Telegraph) ships the original tone assets and a TGCallAudioPlayer-style loop, so the assets and the loop are a cheap port.
tdlib: none - purely local audio; state already comes from updateCall via TGCall handleUpdate:

name: Speaker / audio route toggle during a call
whatItIs: CallControllerButtonsNode plus CallRouteActionSheetItem let the user switch between earpiece, speaker and Bluetooth mid-call.
whyItMatters: TGCallViewController only builds Mute, End and Answer. The audio session is pinned to AVAudioSessionModeVoiceChat (TGCall.mm ~line 429), so there is no way to put a call on speaker - you cannot set the phone down, and with no echo canceller in our libtgvoip build the speaker path also needs to be an explicit, warned-about user choice rather than an accident.
whereItGoes: A third button in TGCallViewController.m next to Mute, calling AVAudioSession overrideOutputAudioPort: (available on iOS 6). A route action sheet on top of TGActionSheet only if Bluetooth is worth it; speaker/earpiece alone covers the real need.

name: Emoji key verification on the call screen
whatItIs: CallControllerKeyButton / CallControllerKeyPreviewNode show the four emoji derived from the call key in the top-right corner; tapping expands them with the 'compare these with your partner' explainer.
whyItMatters: It is the only user-visible proof that the call is end-to-end encrypted and not intercepted, and it was already present in the very first Telegram calls UI. TDLib hands the emoji to us for free: TGCall.mm handleUpdate: reaches callStateReady and passes state straight to startMediaWithState: without ever reading state["emojis"].
whereItGoes: TGCall.h expose an NSArray *keyEmoji populated in handleUpdate:; TGCallViewController.m renders a four-emoji label top-right plus a tap-to-expand panel (the rating panel already establishes the overlay pattern in that file).
tdlib: callStateReady.emojis - already arriving in the update TGCall parses, no new call

name: Recent Calls list
whatItIs: CallListUI is a whole tab: calls grouped by peer and day, incoming/outgoing/missed arrows, missed shown in red, an All/Missed segmented filter, swipe or edit-mode delete, tap to call back, info button to open the chat.
whyItMatters: There is no call history screen at all - nothing in src/ calls -callLogWithOffset:onlyMissed:limit:completion:, -clearCallLogRevoke:, -frequentlyCalledContactsWithCompletion: or -searchCallMessagesOnlyMissed:. A user cannot see who called while the app was closed, cannot call anyone back, and cannot tell a missed call happened. The 2013 client had exactly this tab, so it is period-correct as well as useful.
whereItGoes: A new TGCallListViewController next to TGChatListViewController, reachable from the tab bar / root; rows reuse the avatar+two-line cell pattern of TGContactsViewController. Every field the cell needs (name, date, outgoing, missed, video, duration, ready-made subtitle text) is already returned by the wrapper.
tdlib: searchCallMessages - wrapped twice (TGClient+Calls callLogWithOffset:onlyMissed:limit:completion: and TGClient+Search searchCallMessagesOnlyMissed:)

name: Return-to-call bar when the call screen is dismissed
whatItIs: CallStatusBarNode: a green bar under the status bar showing the running call timer while the user browses chats; tapping it returns to the call screen.
whyItMatters: TGCallViewController is presented as a full-screen modal with no way out except ending the call, so during a call the whole app is unusable - you cannot look up an address or a name mid-conversation, which is the single most common reason to touch the phone while talking.
whereItGoes: A minimize control in TGCallViewController.m plus a small always-on-top UIWindow (windowLevel above status bar) driven by TGCall.state and -duration; presented/hidden from AppDelegate.m where TGWatchForIncomingCalls already owns the call lifecycle.
tdlib: none - TGCall already publishes state and duration

name: Incoming calls while the app is backgrounded or the screen is locked
whatItIs: Modern Telegram receives calls via a VoIP push and CallKit, so the call screen appears even when the app is not running.
whyItMatters: src/Info.plist declares no UIBackgroundModes at all, so TDLib's connection dies on suspend and an incoming call simply never arrives unless the app is in the foreground. That makes voice calling on this client effectively receive-only-while-staring-at-it. iOS 6 does support the `voip` background mode with setKeepAliveTimeout:handler:, which is the pre-PushKit mechanism the era's VoIP apps used and which fits this device.
whereItGoes: Info.plist UIBackgroundModes = voip, plus a keep-alive/reconnect path around the TDLib client in TGClient.m and a call-arrival hook in AppDelegate.m next to TGWatchForIncomingCalls. CallKit and PushKit are unavailable on iOS 6, so the presentation is a local notification plus the existing full-screen controller.
tdlib: updateCall - already handled; the gap is process lifetime, not API

name: Missed-call notification
whatItIs: notificationTypeNewCall / notificationGroupTypeCalls produce a 'Missed call from X' banner and badge that opens the call log.
whyItMatters: Nothing in src/ ever creates a UILocalNotification (only TGClient+Notifications.h mentions the type), so a call missed while the app was not on screen leaves no trace anywhere - no banner, no badge, and, until the Recent Calls list exists, no history either.
whereItGoes: AppDelegate.m alongside TGWatchForIncomingCalls: on callStateDiscarded with reason callDiscardReasonMissed while not active, schedule a UILocalNotification whose userInfo routes to the call log / chat.
tdlib: updateCall callStateDiscarded reason - already parsed in TGCall.mm humanReason:

name: Peer-to-peer calls privacy setting
whatItIs: The privacy screen exposes 'Calls -> Peer-to-Peer' separately from 'Who can call me', letting the user force every call through Telegram's reflectors instead of a direct connection.
whyItMatters: P2P mode reveals your IP address to whoever you talk to; on the modern client turning it off is the standard advice. TGClient+Privacy.m already knows AllowPeerToPeerCalls and even has the display string 'Peer-to-Peer Calls', but TGSettingsViewController.m +privacySettings / +privacyTitles omit it, so it is unreachable.
whereItGoes: Two array literals in TGSettingsViewController.m (around lines 540-556) - add "AllowPeerToPeerCalls" and its title; the existing privacy detail screen handles the rest unchanged.
tdlib: getUserPrivacySettingRules / setUserPrivacySettingRules for userPrivacySettingAllowPeerToPeerCalls - fully wrapped in TGClient+Privacy

name: Call data usage rows
whatItIs: Data and Storage shows bytes sent/received and total airtime spent on calls, with a reset-statistics action.
whyItMatters: On a 2013-era metered plan this is exactly the number a user watches, and calls are the heaviest thing this client does. -callNetworkUsageWithCompletion: and -resetNetworkUsageWithCompletion: are wrapped in TGClient+Calls but nothing in src/ calls either of them.
whereItGoes: A section in TGSettingsViewController.m next to the existing 'Calls' / 'Use less data for calls' group (around line 773), or the storage screen; three static rows plus a destructive reset row.

name: Connection-quality feedback during a call
whatItIs: CallControllerToastNode surfaces 'Weak network signal', 'Your microphone is muted', low-battery and reconnecting states; the modern status node also drives signal bars off the media layer.
whyItMatters: Our call screen shows only a state word and a timer, so a call degrading over EDGE looks identical to a call that is fine, and the user hangs up blaming the app. libtgvoip already reports signal bars and a reconnecting state through its callbacks; TGCall.mm subscribes to neither.
whereItGoes: Wire libtgvoip's signal-bar / state callbacks into TGCall.mm as a published property, and render bars plus a transient toast strip in TGCallViewController.m.

name: 1-to-1 video calls
whatItIs: Full video calling with camera switch, picture-in-picture self view and mid-call upgrade from voice.
whyItMatters: userFullInfo.supports_video_calls is a visible capability on modern peers and the call button offers it; we can only place voice calls.
whereItGoes: Would have to land in TGCall.mm / TGCallViewController.m. It should not: video calls require the tgcalls WebRTC stack with DTLS-SRTP and VP8/H.264 negotiation that our libtgvoip 1-to-1 reflector transport does not implement, and the 4S front camera plus one A5 core and ~50MB of usable RAM cannot encode and decode a live stream alongside the audio path. Record the peer capability so the UI can say 'video calls are not supported on this device' rather than failing obscurely.
tdlib: createCall is_video - would need the media layer, not the API

name: Group calls and video chats (join, even listen-only)
whatItIs: VideoChatScreen / VoiceChatController: joining a channel or group voice chat, participant list with speaking indicators, raise hand, mute others, scheduling, screencast.
whyItMatters: Video chats are how most groups now hold live conversation, and links to them arrive in ordinary chats. We already parse the service messages and can decline an invitation, which is the honest floor.
whereItGoes: Nothing to build. Group calls use an SFU with WebRTC DTLS-SRTP, Opus simulcast and per-participant streams; our media layer is a single-peer libtgvoip reflector connection, and decoding several concurrent audio streams on one A5 core with 512MB is out of reach. whyItMatters: Every chat open in our client makes a network round trip before a single bubble appears (TGClient.m line 1063 hardcodes only_local:NO), which on a 4S over EDGE is seconds of blank screen, and with no connectivity the chat is simply empty even though the messages are in the local database we already enabled. A local pass followed by a remote refresh fixes both.
whereItGoes: TGClient.m -fetchHistoryChunkForChat:... (line 1054): one local call to paint, then the existing remote walk to reconcile; TGChatViewController -reload consumes it unchanged if the completion may fire twice.
tdlib: getChatHistory only_local:true (the parameter is there but pinned to NO)

whatItIs: Chats carry unread_mention_count and unread_reaction_count plus the positions to jump to; the modern chat shows an @-badge that walks through unread mentions and clears them with readAllChatMentions.
whyItMatters: We wrap readAllChatMentions and readAllChatReactions and TGClient+Forums.m already surfaces the per-topic counts, but the main chat never reads the counts, never handles the two updates that maintain them, and has no jump affordance. In a busy group you have no way to find the message that mentioned you - the classic reason to open a group at all.
whereItGoes: TGChatViewController.m next to the existing scroll-down button (-updateScrollDownButton, line ~2076) as a second floating badge; counts from TGClient chat records.

name: Draft preview in the chat list row
whatItIs: A chat with an unsent draft shows a red "Draft:" prefix and the draft text in the subtitle line, overriding the last message.
whyItMatters: Without it there is no way to see from the chat list which conversations still have something half-written; the user has to open every chat to find it. TGClient.m already exposes chat["draft"] and TGSavedMessagesViewController already renders it for topics, so the chat list is the odd one out.
whereItGoes: src/TGChatListViewController.m cell subtitle rendering; data already comes from src/TGClient.m:2350 (info["draft"]) and is documented in src/TGClient+ChatList.h:240.
tdlib: updateChatDraftMessage (already handled in TGClient.m chat info mapping)

whyItMatters: Today saveDraft runs only in -viewWillDisappear (src/TGChatViewController.m:1675). Home-button out of a chat and let iOS 6 jetsam kill the app - which happens constantly on a 512MB 4S - and the typed text is gone. This is the single most common way a draft is lost on this hardware.
whereItGoes: src/AppDelegate.m (applicationDidEnterBackground / applicationWillTerminate) calling into the visible TGChatViewController, or an NSNotification observer added in src/TGChatViewController.m next to restoreDraft.

Anything else - a birthday message next week, a post at 18:00 tomorrow - is impossible. UIDatePicker exists on iOS 6, so the only reason it is missing is that nobody built the sheet.

name: Real scheduled-messages screen with reschedule, edit and delete
whatItIs: The modern client opens the chat in a scheduled mode: the pending messages are shown as normal bubbles, ordered by send time, each with a context menu offering Send Now, Reschedule, Edit and Delete.
whyItMatters: Ours is a flat UIActionSheet listing scheduled messages, and the only action is Send Now (showScheduledMessages / sendScheduledMessageAtIndex in src/TGChatViewController.m). A scheduled message with the wrong time or a typo can only be sent immediately or left to fire wrong - it cannot be moved or cancelled. rescheduleMessage is already wrapped and unused by any UI.
whereItGoes: A new lightweight list screen pushed from the send-options sheet, or reuse of TGChatViewController in a scheduled mode; actions via src/TGMessageActionsSheet.m.

name: Scheduled-messages entry point outside the long-press
whatItIs: When a chat has pending scheduled messages the modern client shows a clock button in the navigation bar so the pending queue is visible and reachable at a glance.
whyItMatters: Our only route to scheduled messages is a long-press on Send, and the row only appears if the list happens to be loaded. A user who scheduled something yesterday has no signal it is still pending and no obvious way back to it.
whereItGoes: src/TGChatViewController.m navigation bar, driven by the existing self.scheduledMessages array populated by loadScheduledMessages.

name: Live refresh when a scheduled message fires or is changed elsewhere
whatItIs: TDLib pushes updateNewMessage / updateDeleteMessages for the scheduled queue and updateChatDraftMessage when another device edits the draft; the modern client reacts to both.
whyItMatters: loadScheduledMessages runs once on open, and restoreDraft is guarded by draftRestored so it never runs twice. A message that fires while the chat is open leaves a stale entry in our list, and a draft typed on another device never appears - or worse, our stale composer text overwrites it on exit.
whereItGoes: The update dispatch in src/TGClient.m plus the handlers in src/TGChatViewController.m (restoreDraft / loadScheduledMessages).

name: Reminders in Saved Messages
whatItIs: In Saved Messages the scheduling UI is relabelled as reminders - "Set a reminder", a reminders list - and the fired message arrives as a notification to yourself.
whyItMatters: This is the cheapest genuinely useful scheduling use case on a phone that is mostly used for messaging, and it is the one place the wording matters: "Schedule Message" to yourself reads as nonsense. The mechanism is identical to what we already have.
whereItGoes: Wording and entry point in src/TGSavedMessagesViewController.m and the send-options sheet in src/TGChatViewController.m when chatId is the self chat.

name: Draft carries formatting, reply target and media caption
whatItIs: A TDLib draftMessage holds a full formattedText with entities, an input_message_reply_to and can survive an attachment caption, not just a plain string.
whyItMatters: We store and restore plain text plus a reply id, and restoreDraft only shows a generic "Reply to message" banner without the quoted message. Bold/link markup and any caption typed under an attachment are silently dropped when the chat is reopened.
whereItGoes: src/TGClient+Messages.m setDraftText/draftForChat (widen to formatted text) and the compose banner restore in src/TGChatViewController.m restoreDraft.
tdlib: setChatDraftMessage with draftMessage.input_message_text.text.entities (currently sent as plain text)

name: Message effects on send
whatItIs: A Premium sender picks an effect next to the send button and the recipient's client plays a full-screen animation over the bubble.
whyItMatters: A user would notice effects arriving from modern clients and nothing happening, but there is no fix: the payload is a TGS/webm animation and effect_id can only be set by an active Premium account.
whereItGoes: Would be the send-options sheet in src/TGChatViewController.m; already catalogued as blocked and correctly so.

name: Priority-aware fetch queue with cancel on scroll-away
whatItIs: FetchManagerImpl keeps one entry per resource with a bag of references, priorities (elevated / user-initiated / visible-index), and cancels a fetch the moment the last reference goes away, so only what is on screen is being pulled and a tapped item jumps the queue.
whyItMatters: Every call site in our app uses TGClient's plain downloadFile:completion: at default priority, and TGRemoteImageView -cancelLoading only flips a local BOOL - the TDLib download keeps running. Fast-scrolling a chat or the contact list queues dozens of avatar and thumbnail fetches that keep competing with the photo the user actually tapped. On EDGE/3G on a 4S this is the difference between a tap opening in seconds and in a minute.
whereItGoes: A new small scheduler owned by TGClient (or a TGFetchQueue in src/), called from TGRemoteImageView.m, TGChatViewController.m, TGMediaViewController.m, TGChatListViewController.m; uses the already-wrapped priority argument.
tdlib: downloadFile with priority 1..32 - wrapped as startDownloadingFile:priority:completion:

name: Per-file transfer status fan-out and in-bubble progress ring
whatItIs: FileMediaResourceStatus / ChatMessageInteractiveMediaBadge model each media as Remote / Fetching(progress) / Local and draw a per-bubble circular progress with a cancel cross, independently for every visible message.
whyItMatters: We have one global TGClient.onFileProgress block. TGChatViewController overwrites it for a single downloadingFileId and shows one centred percentage HUD; TGMediaViewController saves and restores the previous block to avoid clobbering it. Only one transfer can be observed at a time, and a bubble downloading in the background shows nothing. Users cannot see or cancel a second download.
whereItGoes: Replace onFileProgress with a fileId->observers registry in TGClient.m, draw the ring in ChatViewCell.m, delete the HUD in TGChatViewController.m (~line 2308).

name: Download failure surfacing and tap-to-retry
whatItIs: Modern clients turn a failed or cancelled fetch back into the Remote state with a download arrow, so a retry is one tap; TDLib reports the failure through updateFile / the request error.
whyItMatters: Nearly every download callback in our source is `if (path.length == 0) return;` - a failed fetch leaves a spinner or a blank bubble forever with no way to retry short of leaving and re-entering the chat. On a flaky 3G link this is the single most common file-transfer failure a 4S user hits.
whereItGoes: Same status model as the progress ring: ChatViewCell.m plus the completion blocks in TGChatViewController.m, TGMediaViewController.m, TGProfileViewController.m.
tdlib: getFile / fileInfo: to re-check state - wrapped

name: Report the real network type to TDLib
whatItIs: The app watches reachability and calls setNetworkType(wifi/mobile/mobileRoaming/other/none) on every change, which is what makes auto-download limits and the network-usage breakdown mean anything.
whyItMatters: TGClient+Network.m:460 wraps setNetworkType but nothing in the app ever calls it, and there is no reachability observer anywhere in src/. So TDLib assumes one network forever: our per-network auto-download settings and the Wi-Fi vs mobile columns in the data-usage screen are both fiction, and a user on a metered 3G plan gets Wi-Fi-sized auto-downloads.
whereItGoes: SCNetworkReachability observer in AppDelegate.m feeding [TGClient setNetworkTypeKind:]; SystemConfiguration is fine on iOS 6.

name: Keep transfers alive when the app is backgrounded
whatItIs: A background task assertion held while any download or upload is in flight, so pressing Home mid-send does not freeze the transfer.
whyItMatters: There is no beginBackgroundTask anywhere in src/. Sending a photo or pulling a video and then locking the phone suspends the process and the transfer stalls until the user returns - on a 4S over 3G a 10MB video is minutes, so this happens constantly. iOS 6 grants ~10 minutes, which is exactly the window this needs.
whereItGoes: AppDelegate.m applicationDidEnterBackground, driven by the same transfer registry as the progress fan-out.
tdlib: none new; uses the active-transfer set derived from updateFile

name: Play video and music while they download
whatItIs: MediaPlayer / UniversalMediaPlayer feed AVPlayer through a resource loader backed by byte-range fetches, so playback starts on the first seconds instead of the whole file.
whyItMatters: Every video and audio playback path calls the whole-file downloadFile:completion:, so a 20MB video is a multi-minute wait behind a percentage HUD before the first frame. TGClient+Files already exposes the exact primitives a resource loader needs (downloadedPrefixSizeForFile:offset:, downloadFile:offset:limit:, streamFile:offset:count:) and none of them are called from any screen. Only progressive MP4/H.264 is in scope - the 4S cannot decode the modern alternative-quality codecs.
whereItGoes: An AVAssetResourceLoaderDelegate used by TGMediaViewController.m and the audio player; /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/twelve/Telegraph/TGMusicPlayer.m and TGModernConversationAudioPlayer.m already implement this pattern in Objective-C, so the port is mostly plumbing to streamFile:.

name: Free-space guard and disk-full handling on download
whatItIs: Modern clients check available space against the resource size before fetching and surface a clear out-of-space error rather than failing mid-write.
whyItMatters: TGVideoRecorder.m already does exactly this check for recording (freeDiskSpace / diskFloor), but the download side has no equivalent. A 4S that is nearly full silently fails part-way into a big file, and because failures are not surfaced at all the user just sees a stuck bubble.
whereItGoes: Same guard helper reused from TGVideoRecorder.m, applied in the fetch scheduler before startDownloadingFile:, with an offer to run the existing storage cleanup in TGStorageViewController.

name: Cancel an outgoing media send from the bubble
whatItIs: A pending upload shows its progress on the bubble with a cross that aborts the send and removes the message.
whyItMatters: We can start uploads (uploadFileAtPath:, cancelUploadOfFile:) but neither is called from any screen, and the sending bubble shows no progress. On a slow uplink a mis-picked 8MB photo is unstoppable and blocks everything queued behind it.
whereItGoes: ChatViewCell.m sending state plus TGChatViewController.m send path; cancel maps to deleting the pending message, as the header already notes.

name: Preload the neighbouring photo in the media viewer
whatItIs: The gallery fetches the next and previous item at low priority while the current one is on screen, so swiping is instant.
whyItMatters: TGMediaViewController fetches strictly on demand, so every swipe in a photo gallery is a fresh round trip on a link where that is seconds. One low-priority prefetch each side is the cheapest perceived-speed win in the whole file-transfer area, and it is bounded so it costs no memory beyond one extra decoded image.
whereItGoes: TGMediaViewController.m paging callback, using priority 1 for the neighbours and the tapped item at high priority via the fetch scheduler.
tdlib: downloadFile with priority - wrapped as startDownloadingFile:priority:completion:

The existing feature-catalogue entry 'Secret chat search' (area: search) is bucketed blocked with the rationale that this client does not implement E2E sessions -- that rationale is wrong: TDLib performs all the E2E work itself once use_secret_chats is YES, and searchSecretMessages hits only the local DB. The correct bucket is small.

In a secret chat the 'Delete for Me' branch is a lie: the message goes from the peer's device too. A privacy feature that misrepresents what deletion does is worse than not having it.

whereItGoes: The message long-press action sheet in /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/iTgLegacy/src/TGChatViewController.m and the media viewer's save/share buttons; -secretChat:allowsInputMessage: already exists for the inbound direction, this is the missing outbound half. whatItIs: EditThemeController lets a user tweak a theme and share it as a .tgios-theme file or t.me/addtheme link.
whyItMatters: TGThemeFile reads both formats but writes neither, so a palette assembled on this device cannot leave it. Lower value than the rest of this list, but the parser is symmetric and the serialiser is short.
whereItGoes: A +writePalette: counterpart in src/TGThemeFile.m and a 'Share theme' row next to the imported-theme list in TGSettingsViewController.m, handing the file to the existing send-document path.
tdlib: none for the file itself; sending it uses the already-wrapped sendMessage inputMessageDocument

name: System dark-mode following
whatItIs: The .system trigger of AutomaticThemeSwitchTrigger follows UITraitCollection.userInterfaceStyle.
whyItMatters: Listed only so the auto-night screen does not promise it: iOS 6.1.3 has no system-level dark mode and no userInterfaceStyle, so the modern default trigger has no meaning here and the time-based and brightness triggers must carry the whole feature.
whereItGoes: Omit the 'System' option from the auto-night screen in TGSettingsViewController.m.

name: Voice/video note speech transcription
whatItIs: Tap a transcribe glyph on a voice or video note bubble; the server transcribes it and the text appears under the waveform, with a pending spinner and a Good/Bad rating row when it finishes.
whyItMatters: On a 4S in a noisy place, or with a speaker you cannot play out loud, a voice note is currently unreadable. This is the single most useful modern feature we already have fully wrapped and never call from any screen.
whereItGoes: ChatViewCell.m voice/video-note bubble (add a glyph plus a transcript label that grows the cell height), driven from TGChatViewController.m where the message-update callback already refreshes cells; also as a 'Transcribe' row in TGMessageActionsSheet.m.

name: Inline translation under the bubble instead of an alert
whatItIs: Translating a message replaces or appends the translated text inside the bubble itself, with the original still reachable via 'Show Original'. Modern client keeps a per-message translation attribute so it survives scrolling.
whyItMatters: Today TGChatViewController.m -translateMessage: dumps the result into a modal alert, which loses the text the moment you dismiss it and cannot be scrolled or copied comfortably in a conversation.
whereItGoes: TGChatViewController.m:3506 -translateMessage: plus ChatViewCell.m; keep an NSMutableDictionary of messageId -> translated string on the controller and re-lay out the cell.

name: Per-chat 'Translate this chat' bar
whatItIs: A one-line bar under the navigation bar of a chat in a foreign language: 'Translate to English' with a dismiss/settings chevron. Enabling it translates the visible messages in bulk and keeps translating as you scroll.
whyItMatters: Translating message by message through the action sheet is unusable for a real foreign-language conversation. This is the entry point everything else in the cluster hangs off.
whereItGoes: TGChatViewController.m — reuse the existing compose/pinned banner layout above the message list; state persisted per chat via TGClient+Translation -setChat:translatable: and updateChatIsTranslatable.

name: Translation settings: Show Translate Button and Do Not Translate list
whatItIs: A Language section in Settings with a 'Show Translate Button' toggle, a target-language picker, and a multi-select 'Do Not Translate' list of languages the translate bar never offers for.
whyItMatters: Without a do-not-translate list the chat bar nags on every chat whose language detection is fuzzy; without a target picker we can only translate to the phone's locale (hardcoded at TGChatViewController.m:3504).
whereItGoes: New section in TGSettingsViewController.m pushing a plain grouped UITableView language list; values stored in NSUserDefaults (this is a client-side preference, not a TDLib one).
tdlib: no new td_api calls; consumes getLanguagePackInfo names already wrapped for the picker list

whatItIs: Settings > Language lists the official language packs from the server with native names and translation completeness, and switching one re-renders the whole UI from the downloaded strings.

whereItGoes: New TGLanguageViewController pushed from TGSettingsViewController.m. Telegraph already implements the whole screen — /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/twelve/Telegraph/TGLocalizationSelectionController.m plus TGLocalizationSignals.m and TGDownloadLocalizationActor.m — so the list and download half is a cheap port. The expensive half is routing our ~hundreds of hardcoded UI strings through a lookup.

name: t.me/setlanguage deep link handling
whatItIs: Opening a setlanguage link shows a confirmation sheet with the pack's name, string count and completeness, then installs and applies it.

whatItIs: Non-premium accounts get N transcriptions per week; the client reads the remaining count and, when exhausted, shows the 'Transcribe voice messages' premium sheet with a cooldown timer.

whatItIs: Channels whose admins enabled automatic translation serve posts already translated to the reader's language; the client shows the translate bar in the on state by default and honours the chat's auto-translate flag.
whyItMatters: The catalogue marks this blocked, which is wrong — the translation happens server-side, so nothing about the 4S prevents it. The admin-side toggle needs boost level checks (TGClient+Channels.m already reads can_enable_automatic_translation and min_automatic_translation_boost_level), but the viewer side is just honouring a flag.

whatItIs: A Translate action on selected text in the input field and on a user's bio / channel description in the profile.

whyItMatters: Today a link inside a message body is dead text. The only tappable thing is the preview bubble, so any message with a link and no preview (t.me/username, tg:// links, hashtags, @mentions, mailto) cannot be opened at all, and a hidden textUrl never reveals its real target.
whereItGoes: TGChatViewController.m message body label (currently a plain UILabel; ChatViewCell.m still uses a UITextView with dataDetectorTypes, which bypasses openLink: and jumps straight to Safari). Needs a small CoreText/UILabel hit-test label; feed it +[TGClient tappableEntitiesIn:] and call the existing -openLink:.
tdlib: getTextEntities / message formatted_text entities - already wrapped as +[TGClient tappableEntitiesIn:] in TGClient+WebLinks.h (currently unused by any screen)

whatItIs: UrlHandling maps every resolved InternalLinkType onto a screen: public chat/username, chat invite, sticker set, bot start, video chat, story, proxy, language pack, background, folder invite.

Yet we already have every destination screen (profile, invite links, sticker strip, proxy, folders, stories). A tapped t.me/durov should open the profile, not Safari.

whatItIs: Opening a Telegram link from Safari, Mail or another app launches the client and navigates to the target.

whereItGoes: AppDelegate.m -handleOpenURL: (line 244): anything that is not the itglegacy scheme goes to the shared link router above.

whatItIs: While typing a message containing a URL, a panel above the input shows the preview that will be attached, with a close button to disable it, and (modern) small/large media and above-text toggles.

Tapping a text block does nothing; tapping a media block opens the whole article in Safari. For a reader whose point is offline, low-bandwidth reading on a 4S, losing every in-article link is a real loss.

whereItGoes: TGInstantViewController: a right bar button opening the existing TGActionSheet with Share / Open in Safari / Copy Link, a footer cell for viewCount and feedbackLink, and a font-size row backed by NSUserDefaults.
tdlib: getWebPageInstantView - already returns viewCount, feedbackLink, isFull
